Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City

comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the
Management Services Department at (818) 548-4844 during regular business hours.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not

MINUTES
  COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  FEBRUARY 13, 2023 AT 4:00 PM

1.  ROLL CALL
  PRESENT: Commissioners Broussalian, Khojayan, Lambillotte, Perian, Tatiyants,
  Ex Officio Roth and Ex Officio Gonzalez (joined the meeting at 4:44pm).

2.  REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA

a.  Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the February
  13, 2023 Regular Meeting of the Commission on the Status of Women was
  Posted on February 9, 2023 on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.
3.  INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS

a.  Presentation: Armenian Bar Association: Pro Bono Clinic Services
  – Providing Legal Support to Women and Girls in Need, Ida Anbarian

  Presentation by Ida Anbarian, member of the Armenian Bar Association.

  Anbarian presented a brief overview of the Armenian Bar Association’s Pro Bono
  Clinic services provided to the community. Anbarian stated that the clinic
  currently assists about six clients per week with majority of the clients being
  women. The clinic provides assistance to anyone who needs legal services.
  Anbarian stated that a significant portion of the clients consists of low income/
  recent immigrants who speak little to no English. Anbarian stated that the clinic
  is located at the Adult Recreation Center at 201 E Colorado St Glendale, CA
  91205 and the office hours are Saturdays from 10:00am to 12:00 pm. Anbarian
  mentioned that the clinic has assisted eight victims of domestic violence.
  Commissioner Broussalian asked what type of services are provided to the
  clients and the response was preparing and filing restraining orders, locating free
  childcare services, translation services, and helping file for attorneys’ fees.
  Commissioner Perian asked where the clinic obtains funding to provide services
  to the community and the response was that most of the work is volunteer along
  with resources from the City of Glendale CDBG grant program. Commissioner
   Khojayan asked if the clinic helps clients find shelter and the response was that
  the clinic provides a list of organizations located in Glendale that provide shelter
  assistance. Commissioner Tatiyants asked how clients learn about the services
  and the response was that the clinic collaborates with the Glendale Fire
  Department and churches to educate the public about the services provided by
  the clinic. Student Ex officio Roth asked about the number of attorneys working
  at the clinic and the response was two paid attorneys and thirty-five attorneys
  who are volunteers. Chair Lambillotte asked if the clinic represents clients in
  legal proceedings and the response was that the clinic does not represent clients
  in legal proceedings.

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items NOT a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed
  5 minutes. The Commission may question or respond to the speaker but there
  will be no debate or discussion. Staff may refer the matter to the proper
  department for investigation and report.
  Karin Kachler called regarding trauma informed care and physical impact of
  trauma for women and girls who experience domestic violence.
  City Clerk, Suzie Abajian introduced herself and stated that due to staffing
  shortages, the City Clerk’s office has agreed to oversee the Commission on the
  Status of Women. Abajian stated that she is deeply committed to issues
  impacting women in the community. Abajian stated her department is in process
  of hiring an analyst who will be working with the commission directly. All
  commissioners welcomed Dr. Suzie Abajian.

5.  CONSENT ITEMS

a.  Approval of the minutes of the regular Commission Meeting held on
  November 14, 2022

  Motion by Commissioner Broussalian and seconded by Khojayan
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, and Chair Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain: Commissioners Perian and Tatiyants
  Motion passes (3-0-2)

6.  ACTION ITEMS

a.  2023-2026 Strategic Plan
   1. Motion to approve the revised 2023-2026 CSW Strategic Plan prepared by
  the Ad Hoc Committee

  Motion by Commissioner Broussalian and seconded by Tatiyants
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Perian, Tatiyants, and Chair
  Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (5-0-0)

  2. Motion to approve the Strategic Plan be posted on the website of the
  Commission

  Motion by Commissioner Tatiyants and seconded by Broussalian
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Perian, Tatiyants, and Chair
  Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (5-0-0)

  3. Motion to approve a public hearing to be held at the next Commission
  meeting on May 8, 2023 to solicit feedback from community partners and the
  public on how to best implement the plan to meet the needs of the Glendale
  community
  Motion by Commissioner Khojayan and seconded by Broussalian
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Perian, Tatiyants, and Chair
  Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (5-0-0)
b.  Request for Proclamations from the Glendale City Council
  1. Motion Requesting a Proclamation from Glendale City Council Designating
  March 2023 as Women’s History Month, and March 8, 2023 as International
  Women’s Day

  Motion by Commissioner Perian and seconded by Khojayan
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Perian, Tatiyants, and Chair
  Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (5-0-0)
  2. Motion Requesting a Proclamation from Glendale City Council Designating
  April 2023 as Sexual Assault Awareness Month, and April 26, 2023 as Denim
  Day
   Motion by Commissioner Perian and seconded by Khojayan
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Perian, Tatiyants, and Chair
  Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (5-0-0)

c.  Update on Sponsorship of Glendale Unified School District for Yellow
  Ribbon Week: Hands & Words Are Not For Hurting Project
  1. Motion approving the purchase of items for the sponsorship of the Hands
  & Words Project antiviolence program including the allocation of an
  additional amount of $930.50 towards the materials requested by Glendale
  Unified School District
  Motion by Commissioner Khojayan and seconded by Perian
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, Perian, Tatiyants, and Chair
  Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (5-0-0)

7.  REPORTS-INFORMATION ONLY

a.  Legislative Update

  Presented by Kyra Ross, Contract Lobbyist.

8.  COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN/STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioner Khojayan welcomed Commissioner Tatiyants to the commission.
  Student Ex Officio Roth started a girl empowerment program in the community for
  children three years and older. Roth stated that the purpose of the program is to
  introduce the idea of girl empowerment from a young age. Commissioner Perian
  asked to share the date, time, and location of the program and the response was
  that the flyer will be sent to the Commission. Commissioner Tatiyants asked how
  the program is being advertised to the community and the response was by
  speaking to principles at GUSD schools. Roth stated that the library department
  assists with funding for the program.
  City Clerk, Suzie Abajian gave an update regarding the City of Glendale Report
  on the Status of Women. Abajian stated that the Ad Hoc committee is in the
  process of reviewing the current draft and will be giving feedback to MSMU to
  finalize the report. Abajian stated that MSMU will submit the final report to the
  commission on March 31st. Abajian stated that the report will be posted on the
  commission website and will be on the agenda for approval during the May 8th
  meeting. Abajian recommended holding a public hearing for this agenda item
   during the May 8th meeting to solicit input on how to operationalize this report and
  support programming and initiatives that best serve women in our community.

9.  ADJOURNMENT AT 5:04 PM
  Motion by Commissioner Broussalian and seconded by Perian.
